title: Choose the ASCII world
question: The roll assigned The Card Sorter. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Card Sorter
options.lineage: IBM 80-column punched cards and the card sorter
options.thesis: The whole site is a deck of punched cards that sorts itself from scattered to one clean stack as you scroll.
materials: card stock with the pre-printed 0-9 digit field
options.viewport: One full-width card whose digit field punches out EVERY INDUSTRY RUNS ON COMPLEXITY as giant hole-letters, while the interpreter prints the same words along the card's top edge.
options.risk: Can read as nostalgic computing unless the scale and motion feel precise and modern.

raised.raise: Every card carries a visible state, blank to punched to verified, and gets a verifier notch once its section resolves.
Readable text always sits on the nearest plane; glyph fields drift on two slower planes behind it.
Body copy is set in hard, fixed-measure monospace columns instead of floating cards.
Headlines punch at monumental, edge-to-edge scale, with wide quiet fields between sections.

options.label: The Engineering Spec
options.thesis: The site as an authoritative plain-text specification: numbered sections, ASCII system diagrams, page footers.
options.viewport: 1. INTRODUCTION set huge; a diagram of five boxes wiring into one assembles character by character beside it.
options.risk: The familiar developer-docs look; it can feel dry, and many technical sites land here.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Every line of copy is a row of flaps that cascades from noise into words as it arrives.
options.viewport: A full-width board: rows flap into EVERY INDUSTRY RUNS ON COMPLEXITY, and the nine industries are listed like departures.
options.case: Fuses cleanly with 'everything assembles'; loses on audience fit because it reads as travel, not data.
options.risk: Turns gimmicky if the grid is not strict.

options.label: Glyph Render
options.thesis: A live 3D scene drawn in characters: five scattered shards converge into one form, and the copy uses the same glyph ramp.
options.viewport: A rotating glyph sculpture fusing five shards into one, with the headline rendered by the same ramp.
options.case: The purest form of the ASCII idea; loses on audience fit because of its hacker-terminal associations.
options.risk: Glyphs on black is where most ASCII sites land.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: Data lineage told as one ribbon of custody.
options.viewport: One ribbon-led column of dated custody.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a museum frame that buyers don't read as their data world.
options.kept: Known, inferred and verified states stay visible at every step.

options.label: Multiplane Depth
options.thesis: Content on painted planes moving at different speeds.
options.viewport: Planes slide past as the camera sinks through.
options.case: Fuses poorly: storybook, not enterprise data.
options.kept: Text always on the nearest plane, with depth behind it.

options.label: Penny Broadside
options.thesis: One loud printed sheet with dense two-column verse.
options.viewport: A wood-type headline over two rammed columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a satirical folk print.
options.kept: Hard, dense, fixed-measure columns for body copy.

options.label: Flagship Lookbook
options.thesis: Monumental type and vast quiet space.
options.viewport: One enormous word set low on an empty field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: retail luxury with no data story.
options.kept: Monumental scale and wide quiet fields.
options.risk: Says nothing about what ardbergai does.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark AI-consultancy site executed impeccably: headline, network graphic, service cards, industry grid.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, network illustration right, service cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other AI firms, and close to the current site.
